titulo: The passive and impersonal «se»: The pasiva refleja and impersonal «se»

aula.objetivo: Form the passive voice with «ser» + participle (agreeing with the subject), use the passive «se» («Se venden pisos»), impersonal «se» («Se vive bien aquí») and other impersonal forms (third person plural, «uno»), and tell «ser» + participle apart from «estar» + participle.

blocos.titulo: Se venden pisos, se vive bien aquí
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: the passive «se» avoids saying who does the action. It's formed with «se» + verb in the third person — English "is / are + participle" in signs and ads. STEP 2: the verb agrees with the thing that receives the action, which comes after it: «Se vende un piso» (flat for sale), «Se venden pisos» (flats for sale). That's how signs are written: «Se alquila habitación», «Se alquilan habitaciones» (rooms to let). STEP 3: «se» comes before the verb: «Se habla español» (Spanish spoken). STEP 4: impersonal «se» has no subject: the verb is always singular. It's the English generic "you", "one" or "people": «Aquí se vive bien» (Life's good here / You live well here), «En verano se duerme poco», «Se trabaja mucho». STEP 5: when the complement is a specific person, with «a», the verb stays singular: «Se busca a los responsables» (They're looking for those responsible), «Se detuvo a dos sospechosos». Without «a», agreement is required: «Se buscan camareros» (Waiters wanted). STEP 6: don't confuse it with other uses of «se»: reflexive («Ana se lava»), reciprocal («se quieren») and the «se» that replaces «le» before «lo» («se lo di»). Here «se» means "it doesn't matter who". STEP 7: impersonal «se» also goes with «se puede», «se debe», «se necesita»: «Se puede entrar» (You can go in), «No se puede fumar» (No smoking). STEP 8: use «se» for rules and customs: «En España se cena tarde» (In Spain people have dinner late). It's a common generalisation, not true of everybody.
blocos.comparacao: English signs say "Flat for rent", "Rooms to let", "Waiters wanted", "Spanish spoken"; English speech says "you can't smoke here", "people eat late". Spanish covers all of it with «se»: «Se alquila piso», «Se alquilan habitaciones», «Se buscan camareros», «Se habla español», «No se puede fumar», «Se cena tarde». Watch the agreement: plural thing, plural verb.

exemplos.ru: Se habla español, inglés y francés.
En esta calle se cierran las tiendas a las nueve.
exemplos.pt: On this street the shops close at nine.

exemplos.ru: Se necesitan dos camareros para el verano.
exemplos.pt: Two waiters needed for the summer.

exemplos.ru: En verano se duerme la siesta.
exemplos.pt: In summer people take a siesta.

tabela.exemplo: Se busca a la autora del libro.
tabela.traducao: They're looking for the author of the book.

erros.motivo: The thing is plural, so the verb agrees.
English "Spanish is spoken here" is copied as a «ser» passive; natural Spanish uses «se».
With a person and «a», the verb stays singular.

blocos.enunciado: Write and say out loud five short notices with «se», as on a door or in an ad: «Se prohíbe…», «Se alquila…», «Se necesitan…». Then say three customs from your country with «se»: «En mi país se…».
Put into the passive: «La alcaldesa inauguró el museo» and «Una editorial publicará los libros». Then say the participle of «vender», «alquilar» and «prohibir».
